### Automation

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |

| `WJ-019` | Automation levels | ✅ Done | Assist/Guided/Autonomous/Continuous; `resolveCapability` enforces risk-based gating (unit tested). |

| `WJ-021` | Scheduled runs | ✅ Done | List, enable/disable, run now, duplicate, delete. Due schedules now actually fire while the app is open via `services/scheduler.ts` (`SchedulerRunner`, one tick per minute, idempotent: the schedule advances before the run starts). |
| `WJ-022` | Scheduled workflow builder | ✅ Done | `ScheduleBuilder` — trigger/schedule/stages/search/conditions/actions/level/provider. |
| `WJ-023` | Workflow templates | ✅ Done | `services/mock/templates.ts` — 5 templates, duplicate supported. |
| `WJ-024` | Silence/no-op outcome | ✅ Done | Each schedule's condition (`strong_matches > n`, `new_jobs > n`, `always`) is carried on the run and evaluated by `conditionMet()` in the engine (unit tested); unmet → `silent`, no notification; cards say "quiet — nothing to report". |
| `WJ-094` | Server-side cron for scheduled runs | ✅ Done | `GET /api/cron/scheduled-runs` (Vercel Cron, `vercel.json`; `CRON_SECRET` bearer, 503 without one) fires every tenant's due schedules with nobody's tab open. `server/workflow/dueTenants.ts` asks the database which tenants have work (`wonderjobs.due_schedule_tenants`, migration `0004`) instead of pulling every workflow document; `server/workflow/snapshot.ts` loads a tenant's career/jobs/workflow/automation documents in the client's own persisted shape (`server/clientState.ts`) and writes them back with the same trimming the browser's `partialize` applies; `server/workflow/serverExecutors.ts` runs profile → search → dedupe → understand → match → quality → rank through the **same** `WorkflowEngine` the browser uses, against `server/jobs/search.ts`. Stages needing the candidate (prepare, review, apply) are deliberately not run — the shortlist, saved jobs and a notification are waiting when they next sign in. Idempotent by construction: the schedule's `nextRunAt` advances *before* the run starts, so a crash or a timeout can never re-fire in a loop; one run per tenant per tick, skipped while another run is active; per-tenant 60 s and per-invocation 240 s budgets. Schedule times are now evaluated in the schedule's own timezone (`domain/workflow/schedule.ts`, DST-aware, 8 unit tests) — the old `setHours` version would have moved everyone's 08:00 to 08:00 UTC once the cron owned it; the browser uses the same function. Cadence is a deployment fact, not an assumption: Vercel's Hobby plan runs a cron **once a day** (a `*/15` schedule fails the build there), which is a safety net rather than a scheduler, so `vercel.json` ships `0 2 * * *` and the browser keeps firing schedules at their proper time. `CRON_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 1440) declares the real cadence; at or below 60 the cron owns scheduling and the client ticker stands down (`server/workflow/cronCadence.ts`, reported to the browser by `/api/jobs/sources`). They can never double-fire either way: one `isDue` rule — shared by the browser, the cron and the SQL — skips a schedule that already ran in the last 12 hours, which is shorter than the gap between any two legitimate firings this product can express. 7 unit tests cover firing, publishing the catalog, notifying, staying silent when the condition isn't met, advancing on failure, skipping review-only schedules and refusing to start a second concurrent run. |
| `WJ-097` | Follow-up and interview reminders from the server | ✅ Done | The cron's second pass (`server/workflow/reminders.ts`, same `/api/cron/scheduled-runs` invocation) raises the reminders the browser's ticker used to raise only while a tab was open — an interview on Tuesday is exactly what someone needs told to them on Monday. Tenants with something near enough to matter come from `wonderjobs.due_reminder_tenants` (migration `0006`, a jsonb query over applications' follow-ups) instead of reading every tenant's applications. Lead times match the browser's: two days for an interview, one for a follow-up, and still worth saying for a day after it was due. Idempotent through the **same** `career.reminded` list the browser writes, so the two can never raise the same reminder twice, and the career document is merged rather than replaced so a concurrent tab doesn't lose work. Each reminder is also pushed (WJ-096). Reminders run even when the schedule pass has eaten most of the invocation's budget: a missed interview reminder is worse than a late run. 10 unit tests. |

### Platform

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-090` | PWA installability | ✅ Done | `app/manifest.ts` (id, name, `start_url: "/app"`, `display: "standalone"`, shortcuts to Run/Jobs/Applications); icons generated with `next/og`'s `ImageResponse` — `app/icon.tsx` (favicon) and `app/apple-icon.tsx` (iOS) via Next's file convention, plus explicit `app/icon-192.png`, `app/icon-512.png` and `app/icon-512-maskable.png` route handlers so the manifest can reference fixed URLs. `lib/pwa.ts` (`useInstallPrompt`) captures `beforeinstallprompt` and exposes it as "Install app" in the avatar menu — Chromium only; iOS/Firefox have no such API, so the item simply doesn't render there. `public/sw.js` registered in production only (`components/pwa/RegisterServiceWorker.tsx`): deliberately does not cache any page or API response (this app is local-first and real-time already — `store/remoteStorage.ts` — so a caching service worker would risk serving stale job/run/application data), it only serves a small static offline page when a navigation's `fetch` fails. |
| `WJ-096` | Push notification delivery | ✅ Done | Web Push end to end, with no dependency: `server/push/webPush.ts` implements RFC 8291 (ECDH P-256 → HKDF-SHA256 → AES-128-GCM, `aes128gcm` framing) and RFC 8292 (ES256 VAPID JWT, DER→JOSE signature conversion) on `node:crypto`, and the tests **reproduce RFC 8291's own published test vector byte for byte** — a round-trip against our own code would have passed just as happily with the whole chain wrong. Subscriptions live in `wonderjobs.push_subscriptions` (migration `0005`), one row per browser; a 404/410 from a push service means the browser dropped the subscription, so the row is deleted rather than retried forever. `POST/GET/DELETE /api/push/subscribe` (session required, rate-limited, tenant-scoped delete so no account can unsubscribe another's browser); the POST sends a real notification straight away so "it's on" is something the candidate sees. `components/pwa/PushNotifications.tsx` on the Profile page never asks for permission on load — an uninvited prompt is how a site gets blocked permanently, and a blocked browser can't be un-blocked from the page — and the whole card is hidden on deployments with no keys. `public/sw.js` gained `push` and `notificationclick` handlers, the latter reusing an open tab instead of opening a window per notification. Wired into the scheduled-run cron: the in-app notification is saved first and is the record; the push is sent last and can never cost a run its results. Operator setup is `npm run push:keys` plus three environment variables. 17 unit tests. |

### Career DNA

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-095` | Import from resume | ✅ Done | `POST /api/career/import-resume` (session required, rate-limited per tenant, 5 MB cap) takes a PDF, DOCX, plain text or a pasted body and returns a **draft**, never a write: `components/career/ResumeImport.tsx` shows every suggested field with the words it came from, the candidate ticks what to keep, and only then is it applied to the Career DNA form (still unsaved). Offered on `/app/career-dna` and inside onboarding step 2. The file is read in memory and discarded — nothing is stored. Extraction is dependency-free (`server/resume/extractText.ts`): a DOCX is a ZIP read through its central directory and inflated with `node:zlib`; a text PDF is its Flate streams' `Tj`/`TJ` operators, with escapes, octal codes and hex strings decoded and undecodable streams skipped rather than failing the file. A scanned PDF has no text at all, so `looksReadable()` gates the result and the route answers 422 with "paste it instead" rather than returning an empty profile. Parsing (`server/resume/parseResume.ts`) reuses the **same** `SKILL_LEXICON`, `extractSkills` and `inferSeniority` the product uses to read job postings — that shared vocabulary is what makes a skill found in a resume actually match a skill found in a posting. Skill strength follows how often a skill runs through the document; seniority reads only lines that look like held titles ("Reported to the director." is not a directorship); years prefers a stated "N years of experience" over the earliest dated role. Career goal, salary and work modes are deliberately never guessed. 30 unit tests, including PDFs and DOCXs built byte by byte in the tests themselves and the route's multipart, JSON, 415/422/400/401 paths. |
